review: The Arabic repeats 'مَنْ يَا تُرَى مِثْلُ هٰذَا الْحَبِيب؟' as lines 2 and 4 of every stanza, so the Hebrew repeats the same line there; stanza 2 line 2 is a deliberate variant, as in the Arabic.
2:1 מוֹת הַצְּלָב — צְלָב is a post-biblical loan; the biblical alternatives (מוֹת הָעֵץ, תְּלִיָּה) either obscure the cross or mean 'hanging'. Recorded in the glossary.
4:2 זוֹכֵר מְקוֹרֵנוּ — 'remembering our origin', for ذَاكِرًا أَصْلَنَا; מָקוֹר is the biblical word for source/origin.

4:3 וַיַּעְלֵם עֵינוֹ — literally 'hid His eye', i.e. overlooked, for وَحَجَبَ الطَّرْفَ. The idiom הֶעֱלִים עַיִן is rabbinic rather than biblical, but it is the only Hebrew phrase that keeps the image.
